units.text: INT. BARBARA - CONTINUOUS
That's right.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: To Barbara.
So you are coming to see my death and devastation factory, Barbara?
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: BARBARA [at the window] You came yesterday to see my salvation factory.
I promised you a return visit.
LOMAX [coming forward between Sarah and Undershaft] You'll find it awfully interesting.

I've been through the Woolwich Arsenal; and it gives you a ripping feeling of security, you know, to think of the lot of beggars we could kill if it came to fighting. [To Undershaft, with sudden solemnity] Still, it must be rather an awful reflection for you, from the religious point of view as it were.
You're getting on, you know, and all that.
You don't mind Cholly's imbecility, papa, do you?
units.name: SARAH

units.text: LOMAX [much taken aback] Oh I say!
Mr Lomax looks at the matter in a very proper spirit, my dear.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: Just so. That's all I meant, I assure you.
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: Are you coming, Stephen?
units.name: SARAH

units.text: Well, I am rather busy--er--
units.name: STEPHEN

units.text: Magnanimously.
Oh well, yes: I'll come. That is, if there is room for me.
units.name: STEPHEN

units.text: I can take two with me in a little motor I am experimenting with for field use. You won't mind its being rather unfashionable. It's not painted yet; but it's bullet proof.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: LOMAX [appalled at the prospect of confronting Wilton Crescent in an unpainted motor] Oh I say!
The carriage for me, thank you. Barbara doesn't mind what she's seen in.
units.name: SARAH

units.text: I say, Dolly old chap: do you really mind the car being a guy? Because of course if you do I'll go in it. Still--
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: I prefer it.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: Thanks awfully, old man. Come, Sarah.
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: He hurries out to secure his seat in the carriage.
Sarah follows him.
moodily walking across to Lady Britomart's writing table.
Why are we two coming to this Works Department of Hell? that is what I ask myself.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: I have always thought of it as a sort of pit where lost creatures with blackened faces stirred up smoky fires and were driven and tormented by my father? Is it like that, dad?
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: UNDERSHAFT [scandalized] My dear!
It is a spotlessly clean and beautiful hillside town.
With a Methodist chapel? Oh do say there's a Methodist chapel.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: There are two: a primitive one and a sophisticated one. There is even an Ethical Society; but it is not much patronized, as my men are all strongly religious. In the High Explosives Sheds they object to the presence of Agnostics as unsafe.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: And yet they don't object to you!
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: Do they obey all your orders?
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: I never give them any orders. When I speak to one of them it is "Well, Jones, is the baby doing well? and has Mrs Jones made a good recovery?" "Nicely, thank you, sir." And that's all.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: But Jones has to be kept in order. How do you maintain discipline among your men?
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: I don't. They do. You see, the one thing Jones won't stand is any rebellion from the man under him, or any assertion of social equality between the wife of the man with 4 shillings a week less than himself and Mrs Jones! Of course they all rebel against me, theoretically. Practically, every man of them keeps the man just below him in his place. I never meddle with them. I never bully them. I don't even bully Lazarus. I say that certain things are to be done; but I don't order anybody to do them. I don't say, mind you, that there is no ordering about and snubbing and even bullying. The men snub the boys and order them about; the carmen snub the sweepers; the artisans snub the unskilled laborers; the foremen drive and bully both the laborers and artisans; the assistant engineers find fault with the foremen; the chief engineers drop on the assistants; the departmental managers worry the chiefs; and the clerks have tall hats and hymnbooks and keep up the social tone by refusing to associate on equal terms with anybody. The result is a colossal profit, which comes to me.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: CUSINS [revolted] You really are a--well, what I was saying yesterday.
What was he saying yesterday?
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: Never mind, my dear. He thinks I have made you unhappy. Have I?
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: Do you think I can be happy in this vulgar silly dress? I! who have worn the uniform. Do you understand what you have done to me? Yesterday I had a man's soul in my hand. I set him in the way of life with his face to salvation. But when we took your money he turned back to drunkenness and derision.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: With intense conviction.

I will never forgive you that. If I had a child, and you destroyed its body with your explosives--if you murdered Dolly with your horrible guns--I could forgive you if my forgiveness would open the gates of heaven to you. But to take a human soul from me, and turn it into the soul of a wolf! that is worse than any murder.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: Does my daughter despair so easily? Can you strike a man to the heart and leave no mark on him?
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: BARBARA [her face lighting up] Oh, you are right: he can never be lost now: where was my faith?
Oh, clever clever devil!
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: You may be a devil; but God speaks through you sometimes.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: She takes her father's hands and kisses them.
You have given me back my happiness: I feel it deep down now, though my spirit is troubled.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: You have learnt something. That always feels at first as if you had lost something.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: Well, take me to the factory of death, and let me learn something more. There must be some truth or other behind all this frightful irony. Come, Dolly.
units.name: BARBARA
